task.title: Behaviour-preserving refactor of kvparse.parser
task.statement: Refactor kvparse/parser.py without changing any behaviour. Two changes are requested. (1) parse_line(line) must be rewritten without the hand-rolled index loops: split the line at the first '=' with str.partition, strip the key and the value, raise ValueError when there is no '=' or the stripped key is empty, and remove one pair of matching surrounding quotes (both ends '"' or both ends "'") from a stripped value of length two or more; the function must not contain a 'while' loop. (2) Extract the detection of ignorable lines into a module-level function _is_ignorable(line) -> bool in kvparse/parser.py that returns True exactly when the stripped line is empty or starts with '#' or ';', and make parse use it. The observable behaviour of parse and parse_line must stay byte-for-byte identical for every str input: the same return values, the same exception types in the same situations (TypeError for non-string input to parse, ValueError for a malformed line), later duplicate keys still win, and quotes are removed only when the stripped value starts and ends with the same quote character (a value like '"x\'' keeps both characters; a lone '"' is kept). Exception messages are not prescribed. parse keeps raising TypeError for non-string input; what parse_line does with a non-string argument (for example a list or a mapping) is unspecified and must not be tested, because the required use of str.partition changes it. Keep the public names parse and parse_line exported from kvparse, do not modify the tests, and keep the existing suite passing.
acceptance_criteria: parse_line raises ValueError for '', 'novalue', ' = v', '   ', '=' and '\t= 1'.

parse behaviour unchanged: comments ('#' or ';' as the first non-blank character), blank lines and Windows line endings are handled as before; later duplicate keys win; parse('') == {}; parse('k = v') == {'k': 'v'}.
parse raises ValueError for a malformed line anywhere in the text and TypeError for non-string input (None, 3, a list, bytes).
kvparse.parser._is_ignorable exists, returns True for '   # c', '' and '\t; c', and False for 'a = 1' and 'a = # not a comment'.
The source of parse_line contains no 'while' loop and uses str.partition.
The existing tests in tests/ pass unchanged.
Unspecified, not to be tested: parse_line with a non-string argument.

spec.restated_task: Refactor kvparse/parser.py while preserving its string-input behavior: replace parse_line's index loops with partitioning at the first '=', retain whitespace stripping, validation and removal of exactly one matching outer quote pair, and extract blank/comment-line detection into a module-level _is_ignorable helper used by parse. Preserve public exports, parsing order, duplicate-key handling and specified exception types; leave existing tests unchanged.

interface_contract.name: kvparse.parser.parse_line (also exported as kvparse.parse_line)
interface_contract.behavior: For a string argument, partition at the first '=' using str.partition. Strip the key and value using default str.strip whitespace semantics. Return a two-element tuple (key, value). If the stripped value has length at least two and its first and last characters are both single quotes or both double quotes, remove exactly those two characters. Preserve all remaining characters, including whitespace inside removed quotes, additional '=' characters and internal quotes. Do not interpret comments or escape sequences. The function must contain no while loop.
error_cases: ValueError: the input string contains no '='.
ValueError: the key before the first '=' is empty after stripping.
Non-string arguments are outside the contract and must not be tested.

interface_contract.name: kvparse.parser.parse (also exported as kvparse.parse)
interface_contract.behavior: Require isinstance(text, str). Iterate over text.splitlines() in order, skipping lines identified by _is_ignorable. Parse each remaining original line with parse_line and assign its key and value into a dict. Return that dict; later occurrences of a key overwrite its value without changing the existing dict insertion-order behavior. Empty text and text containing only ignored lines return {}.
error_cases: TypeError: text is not an instance of str, including None, integers, lists and bytes.
ValueError: any non-ignored line lacks '=' or has an empty stripped key.

interface_contract.name: kvparse.parser._is_ignorable
interface_contract.behavior: For a string line, return a bool that is True exactly when line.strip() is empty or starts with '#' or ';'; otherwise return False. Define this helper at module scope in kvparse/parser.py and have parse use it to decide which lines to skip. No package-level export is required.
error_cases: Non-string arguments are outside the helper's contract; no exception behavior is prescribed for them.

acceptance_criteria: 1. parse_line('a=b') == ('a', 'b'), parse_line(' a = b ') == ('a', 'b'), parse_line('a==b') == ('a', '=b'), parse_line('a = b = c') == ('a', 'b = c'), and parse_line('a=') == ('a', '').
2. parse_line('q = "x"') == ('q', 'x'), parse_line("q = 'x'") == ('q', 'x'), parse_line("q = ''") == ('q', ''), and parse_line('q = ""') == ('q', '').
3. parse_line('q = "x\'') == ('q', '"x\''), and parse_line('q = "') == ('q', '"'). Mismatched outer quotes and lone quote characters remain unchanged.

4. parse_line('q = " spaced "') == ('q', ' spaced '), parse_line('k e y = v') == ('k e y', 'v'), and parse_line('u = "a" "b"') == ('u', 'a" "b'). Remove only one matching outer quote pair; do not strip again afterward or decode escapes.

5. parse_line raises ValueError for each of '', 'novalue', ' = v', '   ', '=' and '\t= 1'. More generally, a string line is malformed exactly when it has no '=' or its prefix before the first '=' strips to an empty key.

6. All string parsing retains default Python str.strip semantics, including Unicode whitespace. parse_line treats line-break characters as ordinary characters subject to boundary stripping, rather than splitting its argument into lines.

7. _is_ignorable returns True for '', whitespace-only strings, '   # c' and '\t; c'; it returns False for 'a = 1' and 'a = # not a comment'. For every string line, its result equals whether the stripped line is empty or begins with '#' or ';'.

8. parse('') == {}, parse('k = v') == {'k': 'v'}, and parse('# comment

9. parse retains str.splitlines() line-boundary behavior, including LF, CRLF, lone CR and other boundaries supported by that method. For example, parse('a=1\r\nb=2\r\n') == {'a': '1', 'b': '2'}.
10. parse('a=1\nb=2\na=3') returns {'a': '3', 'b': '2'} with iteration order ['a', 'b']; stripped keys determine duplicate identity.

limitations: Profile 'eval-attest-a1': inference provider codex_gateway; submission runs must use NVIDIA Nemotron on Nebius Token Factory and are labeled separately.

Sealed and adversarial suites run one child process per test under a supervisor that never imports candidate code and is the first step of its branch; two verifier canaries detect blanket result forgery. A candidate can still forge its own result from inside a child after the nonce was read if it spares the canaries (the mutation gate and held-out tests are the structural detectors).

The repository's own suite and the held-out suite run after the sealed verification in their own branches. They are bound through the same supervisor only for unittest repositories whose tests are statically discoverable; otherwise they are parsed from console output and the gate is labelled evidence_class 'stdout'.

Model-written sealed and adversarial tests can be wrong; their failures block VERIFIED. An independent arbiter classifies each failure (implementation bug, test defect or contract dispute) and, for pure test defects, offers a corrected module. The correction counts only after mechanical validation (same test methods, only the failing ones changed, passes on the candidate, still fails on the unmodified base or is caught by a mutant); the corrected gate is then re-run and the verdict re-derived from the gates. A sealed test that failed by assertion or by an exception raised in the code under test is never overridden (only a test-internal crash or a timeout may be corrected). The classification itself remains a model judgement.

INFEASIBLE is recorded only when a witness program written by the contract auditor demonstrated the contradiction by running on the unmodified repository (exit code and output recorded); the witness's logic is the model's, its execution is not.
Grounding runs only when the specification names external references; sources are cited, not verified for correctness.
